title: checkpointed runbook transcripts and telemetry digests
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: On-call teams often need a compact, replayable artifact that ties a human-run runbook transcript to the exact telemetry slices that were relevant during each decision point. This PR introduces a checkpointed runbook transcript format plus a parallel telemetry digest extractor so that on-call handoffs and postmortems can reference small deterministic artifacts instead of full trace dumps.

What this PR does: Adds a new `slo-toolkit` utility `runbook-compiler` that: 1) consumes a runbook transcript (terminal/chat/incident-bot log) and inserts lightweight checkpoints at operator-confirmed decision points; 2) produces a companion telemetry digest (filtered traces, metrics windows, and top logs) based on timestamp ranges around each checkpoint; 3) emits a compact JSONL artifact with stable IDs for checkpoints that can be referenced from playbooks, incident timelines, and RCA templates.

Design notes: - Checkpoints are detected by a small set of heuristics (explicit `/checkpoint` markers, action verbs plus confirmation tokens, and an optional manual annotation UI hook). Heuristics are intentionally conservative to avoid noise. - The telemetry digester uses pre-existing telemetry sampling hooks in the toolkit to pull metric slices and the minimal set of spans/logs that changed across the checkpoint window. It supports both synthetic sampling (for high-cardinality spans) and deterministic range extraction (when full traces exist). - The artifact schema is stable v1: metadata, ordered checkpoints (id, timestamp, actor, brief summary), telemetry_digests (checkpoint_id -> list of telemetry slices), and an attachments array for screenshots/links.

Backward compatibility and safety: The new binaries are opt-in and do not change any existing runbook formats. The extractor runs with a read-only telemetry API key and respects sampling budgets. There's a feature flag for conservative mode (smaller telemetry windows) which is the default for orgs with large trace volumes.

Testing and verification: - Unit tests for checkpoint detection and schema validation. - Integration tests for end-to-end artifact generation against a replay harness (recorded incident trace). - Benchmarked telemetry digest extraction time: median 210ms per checkpoint on dev infra (see /benchmarks/runbook-digest).

Usage example (one-line): `rt-compile --input incident-2026-02-12.log --out compact-artifact-2026-02-12.jsonl --telemetry-key-file /secrets/tkey --conservative`
